context:
Two parallel streams gated on the ADR addendum (w1) and the
closed-set enum changes (w3, w4):

- Coverage stream (w2 → w5): audit PK enforcement on every supported
  platform with NoConstraintEnforcementMixin as a cross-check, then
  register the missing INFORMATIONAL rules and delete the legacy_bypass
  fallback tuple. Closes the silent-corruption window. Cannot start
  until w3 lands (uses the new INFORMATIONAL name from day one).

- Enum stream (w3 → w4): rename DEGRADED → INFORMATIONAL atomically,
  then split SKIPPED → SKIPPED_QUERY + SKIPPED_DDL_FRAGMENT atomically.
  Sequenced rather than combined so each is a single, individually-
  revertable closed-set transformation.

Then sequenced tail (w6 → w7 → w8 → w9):
- w6: migrate existing SKIPPED rules to refined values.
- w7: reason-string convention + warn-only lint, after w5 and w6 so
  reason updates touch each rule file once.
- w8: generator restructure into two doc sections.
- w9: final docs regeneration + verification.

Mirror the original pipeline's discipline: ADR before code, structural
change before content migration, convention before enforcement,
generator change before doc commit. Keep each enum change atomic - the
enum is a closed set so dual-run / shadow-mode is not feasible. The
reason-string lint stays warn-only in this TODO; promotion to error
mode is a separate follow-up after every rule complies.
description:
After build-sql-compat-phase-aware-pipeline shipped (w17/w18, 2026-04-26),
reviewing the eight skip/block/degrade rows in docs/compat/skip-reference.md
surfaced five problems with the as-shipped support_level surface. Three are
readability gaps; one is a real silent-corruption window the pipeline was
supposed to close; one is a naming choice that biases readers toward the
wrong interpretation.

1. SupportLevel.DEGRADED carries performance-regression connotations and
   reads as a judgement on the platform. The actual semantic - "the
   workload runs end-to-end, but a documented platform-level guarantee
   (typically PRIMARY KEY uniqueness) is not provided" - is closer to how
   vendors document this themselves. Snowflake, Redshift, BigQuery, and
   Databricks docs use INFORMATIONAL or NOT ENFORCED. Renaming
   DEGRADED → INFORMATIONAL aligns with vendor terminology and removes
   the false suggestion that the platform is performing badly.

2. SupportLevel.SKIPPED is overloaded. The same enum value covers
   full-query exclusion (StarRocks vector_search Q2 is dropped from the
   result set entirely on platform_version < 3.2) and DDL-fragment
   suppression (DataFusion write_primitives / transaction_primitives
   lock-table DDL is skipped, but the workload itself runs end-to-end).
   The user-visible consequences are categorically different - one
   removes a query from the benchmark; the other only drops an internal
   coordination DDL - but the doc says "SKIPPED" for both.

3. Rule reason strings explain the platform deficiency ("DataFusion does
   not support PRIMARY KEY syntax", "QuestDB has no VECTOR column type")
   but not the user-visible consequence (benchmark refused at preflight /
   query omitted from results / workload runs with documented caveat).
   Readers consistently misread DDL-fragment skips as full-benchmark skips.

4. The generated skip-reference.md collapses BLOCKED, SKIPPED, and
   DEGRADED into a single per-platform table. Splitting "Will not run"
   (preflight refused or query omitted) from "Runs with caveats" (DDL
   fragment dropped, semantic enforcement gap) would make the page
   self-explaining.

5. PRIMARY KEY enforcement coverage is incomplete. Only four platforms
   have PK-capability rules registered (datafusion, clickhouse,
   starrocks, doris). Every other platform that accepts PRIMARY KEY DDL
   but does not enforce uniqueness silently breaks the
   write_primitives / transaction_primitives setup-lock semantics: the
   CREATE TABLE for write_primitives_setup_lock succeeds, both lock
   INSERTs succeed because uniqueness is not enforced, and concurrent
   setup workers think they own the lock at the same time. The
   legacy_bypass tuple in core/write_primitives/benchmark.py:62 is the
   fallback when no rule resolves; it lists exactly the four covered
   platforms, leaving Snowflake, Redshift, BigQuery, Databricks, Synapse,
   Fabric Warehouse, Firebolt, Spark/PySpark, Trino/Presto/Athena/
   Starburst, Databend, and any other "accepts PK DDL, does not enforce"
   platform without protection.

Critical cross-reference for the audit: benchbox/platforms/base/no_constraint_mixin.py
defines NoConstraintEnforcementMixin, used by DataFusion, Polars, and cuDF.
Adapters using this mixin no-op apply_constraint_configuration at runtime,
meaning even if the registry resolved a NATIVE PK rule, the constraint
would never actually be applied. The mixin is direct, in-tree evidence of
"this platform does not enforce PK constraints". The w2 audit must use
it as a cross-check: every NoConstraintEnforcementMixin user must
classify as INFORMATIONAL (uniqueness not enforced but DDL accepted) or
SKIPPED_DDL_FRAGMENT (parser refuses DDL outright, like DataFusion).
Registering a NATIVE PK rule for a mixin user would be a parity bug.

This TODO addresses all five. The naming change (1) lands as a
closed-set enum rename. The structural change (2) lands as an enum
split with an ADR addendum and rule migration. The convention change
(3) lands as a reason-string format plus a lint check. The doc change
(4) is a generator restructure plus regenerated docs. The PK coverage
gap (5) lands as a per-platform audit followed by INFORMATIONAL rule
registrations and removal of the legacy_bypass tuple.

Coverage and taxonomy work proceed mostly in parallel after the ADR
addendum (w1) and the DEGRADED→INFORMATIONAL rename (w3); coverage
closes the bug-shaped gap; taxonomy is layered on after.

anti_patterns.dont: classify a platform as INFORMATIONAL in w2 based on 'common knowledge' or 'looks like Snowflake'
anti_patterns.instead: every classification must cite a vendor-doc URL or a reproducer
anti_patterns.why: vendor enforcement semantics shift between releases and connector layers (e.g. Trino-on-Iceberg differs from Trino-on-Hive)

anti_patterns.dont: combine the DEGRADED→INFORMATIONAL rename (w3) and the SKIPPED split (w4) into one work unit
anti_patterns.instead: ship them as two sequenced, individually-revertable commits
anti_patterns.why: both are closed-set transformations on the same enum file and combining doubles the diff and the revert blast radius

anti_patterns.dont: couple the coverage stream (w2/w5) to the SKIPPED-split stream (w4/w6)
anti_patterns.instead: the coverage stream depends only on w3 (the rename), not on w4
anti_patterns.why: that delays closing the silent-corruption window behind metadata refactoring

anti_patterns.dont: delete SupportLevel.DEGRADED or SupportLevel.SKIPPED without migrating every caller in the same change set
anti_patterns.instead: audit `grep -rn 'SupportLevel.DEGRADED' benchbox/ tests/ scripts/` (and the same for SKIPPED) before editing decision.py and fix every site in the same commit
anti_patterns.why: Python enums are closed sets and a half-migrated state will not import

anti_patterns.dont: delete the legacy_bypass tuple in benchmark.py before every w2-surfaced platform has a registered rule
anti_patterns.instead: delete the tuple as the LAST step of w5 after the parity test passes
anti_patterns.why: a half-migration leaves uncovered platforms with neither the legacy fallback nor a registry rule, fail-closed instead of fail-open

anti_patterns.dont: extend SupportLevel with a third skip value (e.g. SKIPPED_AUXILIARY) without ADR addendum sign-off
anti_patterns.instead: if a rule does not fit, raise it in w1 before code lands
anti_patterns.why: the taxonomy was deliberately frozen at four outcomes (BLOCKED / SKIPPED_QUERY / SKIPPED_DDL_FRAGMENT / INFORMATIONAL)

anti_patterns.dont: promote the reason-string lint from warn to error in the same slice that introduces the convention
anti_patterns.instead: ship warn-only here, promote in a follow-up
anti_patterns.why: the lint and the rule audit must land atomically if it is error-mode and that doubles the diff

anti_patterns.dont: regenerate docs/compat/*.md in a work unit that also changes the rule registry
anti_patterns.instead: always end the workstream with a clean docs-only regeneration commit (w9)
anti_patterns.why: a single commit then mixes 'registry change' with 'doc shape change' and reviewers cannot tell which drove which

anti_patterns.dont: register PK rules in w5 without first completing the w2 audit
anti_patterns.instead: every w5 rule must cite the audit row that justifies its bucket
anti_patterns.why: guessing at vendor enforcement semantics is exactly how silent-corruption originates

anti_patterns.dont: register a NATIVE PK rule for any adapter that inherits from NoConstraintEnforcementMixin
anti_patterns.instead: mixin members must classify as INFORMATIONAL or SKIPPED_DDL_FRAGMENT and the w5 parity test enforces this
anti_patterns.why: the mixin no-ops apply_constraint_configuration so the constraint never actually gets applied at runtime, registering NATIVE would create a registry/adapter parity bug

anti_patterns.dont: touch _pk_lock_bypass_required logic beyond removing the legacy_bypass tuple
anti_patterns.instead: if a rule cannot be expressed under the existing CompatAction values, raise it in w1, not w5
anti_patterns.why: the function is a stable consumer of the registry and changing its dispatch shape is out of scope

preserves.behavior: Every adapter inheriting from benchbox/platforms/base/no_constraint_mixin.NoConstraintEnforcementMixin resolves to a non-NATIVE PK rule after w5 - this is the structural parity guarantee the new test in w5 enforces
Existing tests under tests/unit/sql_compat/ continue to pass; if a test pins SupportLevel.DEGRADED or SupportLevel.SKIPPED it must be migrated to the appropriate new value, not deleted
Newly-registered INFORMATIONAL PK rules in w5 do not change behavior on the four already-covered platforms (datafusion, clickhouse, starrocks, doris) - their existing rules remain authoritative
NoConstraintEnforcementMixin behavior in benchbox/platforms/base/no_constraint_mixin.py is unchanged; the runtime no-op is a separate concern from the registry rule and remains as-is

REGISTRY.resolve() / resolve_all() / resolve_platform_rules() return decisions with the same action and payload for the same contexts after the rename and split - only the support_level enum value changes; reason strings change only in w7

The two existing DEGRADED rules (starrocks, doris) at write_primitives + transaction_primitives keep their action (REWRITE_DDL), payload (PKCapabilityPayload contents), and reason text after the w3 rename - only support_level renames

_pk_lock_bypass_required in core/{write,transaction}_primitives/benchmark.py continues to short-circuit lock acquire/release for every platform that resolves to a non-NATIVE PK rule (single-process behavior unchanged on covered platforms)
make compat-docs-check exits 0 after w9 and continues to be wired into .github/workflows/lint.yml
scripts/compat_lint.py continues to error on unregistered dialect branches in benchbox/core/ (the existing W16 acceptance gate)

work_units.notes:
Append an addendum to docs/development/adr/adr-sql-compat-phase-aware-pipeline.md
(or land a follow-on ADR that supersedes the relevant section) covering:
(a) the PK-coverage policy: every platform supported by BenchBox that
can host write_primitives / transaction_primitives must have a
registered PK-capability rule (NATIVE, REWRITTEN, SKIPPED_DDL_FRAGMENT,
or INFORMATIONAL) - no fallback to the legacy_bypass tuple is
acceptable after w5 closes; (b) the four SupportLevel outcomes for
this taxonomy revision - BLOCKED (preflight refusal), SKIPPED_QUERY
(query omitted from result set), SKIPPED_DDL_FRAGMENT (auxiliary DDL
dropped, workload runs), INFORMATIONAL (workload runs but a documented
platform guarantee is not provided); (c) the rationale for renaming
DEGRADED → INFORMATIONAL: vendor-aligned terminology (Snowflake,
Redshift, BigQuery use this exact word in their docs), no
performance-regression connotation; (d) the SupportLevel migration
table - DEGRADED → INFORMATIONAL for the two existing rules
(starrocks, doris); SKIPPED → SKIPPED_QUERY or SKIPPED_DDL_FRAGMENT
for each currently-SKIPPED rule; (e) the reason-string convention
(lead with user-visible consequence, then platform-deficiency cause);
(f) the doc-restructure plan for skip-reference.md;
(g) the NoConstraintEnforcementMixin cross-check policy: every
platform adapter using benchbox/platforms/base/no_constraint_mixin.py
must resolve to a non-NATIVE PK rule.
Blocking step - all subsequent work units cite the addendum.
work_units.summary: ADR addendum: PK coverage policy + INFORMATIONAL rename + revised skip taxonomy + reason-string convention

work_units.notes:
Research-only work unit (no code change). For each platform under
benchbox/platforms/ that supports write_primitives /
transaction_primitives, classify PK behavior into one of four
buckets and cite a vendor-doc URL or test repro for each:
(a) NATIVE - parser accepts PK DDL AND uniqueness is enforced
    (DuckDB, PostgreSQL line, MySQL/SingleStore, SQLite, MotherDuck,
    CedarDB, pg_duckdb, pg_mooncake, TimescaleDB);
(b) REWRITTEN - parser accepts PK DDL but it is engine-internal
    metadata, not a constraint (ClickHouse - already registered);
(c) INFORMATIONAL - parser accepts PK DDL but uniqueness is not
    enforced (StarRocks, Doris already registered; Snowflake,
    Redshift, BigQuery, Databricks Delta, Synapse, Fabric Warehouse,
    Firebolt, Spark/PySpark, Trino/Presto/Athena/Starburst, Databend
    candidates);
(d) SKIPPED_DDL_FRAGMENT - parser refuses PK DDL outright
    (DataFusion already registered).
The audit MUST cross-check benchbox/platforms/base/no_constraint_mixin.py:
every adapter inheriting from NoConstraintEnforcementMixin (currently
DataFusion, Polars, cuDF) is in-tree evidence of "PK uniqueness not
enforced" and must classify into bucket (c) or (d). Polars and cuDF
are DataFrame platforms - flag them in the audit as out-of-scope for
SQL-mode primitives but ensure that if any future DataFrame primitives
benchmark uses the registry, the rule is already in place.
Deliver _project/compat/pk_audit.md with one row per platform:
platform_key | bucket | uses_no_constraint_mixin | failure_mode |
conditions | doc_url. The audit must cite first-party documentation
or a reproducer; "common knowledge" is not acceptable evidence.
Out-of-bucket findings (a platform that does not fit any of the four)
must be raised back to w1 for ADR amendment, not silently classified.
work_units.summary: Audit PK enforcement on every BenchBox-supported platform; produce a per-platform classification table

work_units.notes:
Closed-set enum change. Steps:
(a) Edit benchbox/sql_compat/decision.py: rename the DEGRADED member
to INFORMATIONAL (preserving its string value or updating the string
value to "INFORMATIONAL" - decide in w1 ADR addendum, default to
string-value change for vendor alignment).
(b) Update benchbox/sql_compat/__init__.py exports if any reference
DEGRADED.
(c) `grep -rn 'SupportLevel\.DEGRADED' benchbox/ tests/ scripts/`
and migrate every site in the same change set - registry rules
(currently 2: starrocks + doris write_primitives + transaction_primitives,
so 4 rule registrations total), tests, generator, lint script, any
governance code.
(d) If the doc generator filters or labels rows by support_level
string, update those filters too.
(e) Run `uv run -- python -m pytest tests/unit/sql_compat -m fast`
until green. Commit only when the enum module + every caller compile
and pass tests cleanly.
Sequenced before w4 (PK coverage register) so w4 can register new
rules using INFORMATIONAL from day one rather than registering as
DEGRADED and renaming later.
work_units.summary: Rename SupportLevel.DEGRADED → SupportLevel.INFORMATIONAL across the codebase

work_units.notes:

replace SKIPPED with the two refined values. Update __init__.py
exports. Audit all callers of SupportLevel.SKIPPED in benchbox/
(resolver.py, plan.py, any governance / inventory code, tests) and
pick the right replacement based on the rule shape - the enum is a

in tight succession; commit only when the enum module + every caller

work_units.summary: Split SupportLevel.SKIPPED into SKIPPED_QUERY and SKIPPED_DDL_FRAGMENT

work_units.notes:
Extend benchbox/sql_compat/rules/schema_emit/pk_capability.py and
pk_capability_txn.py with one rule per platform from the w2 audit
that does not already have a registered rule. Each rule uses the
bucket assigned in w2 - INFORMATIONAL is the expected default for
the cloud DW class. Payload must use PKCapabilityPayload with
structural fields - ddl_accepted, uniqueness_enforced, conditions,
failure_mode_detail - not a bare boolean. After registration, the
legacy_bypass tuple in core/write_primitives/benchmark.py:62 and
core/transaction_primitives/benchmark.py becomes dead code path;
delete it and gate _pk_lock_bypass_required entirely on
REGISTRY.resolve(). Add tests/unit/sql_compat/test_pk_coverage_parity.py
with two assertions:
(a) every platform in the BenchBox platform registry's
write_primitives-supported set resolves to a non-None PK rule;
(b) every adapter inheriting from
benchbox.platforms.base.no_constraint_mixin.NoConstraintEnforcementMixin
resolves to a PK rule whose support_level is INFORMATIONAL or
SKIPPED_DDL_FRAGMENT (never NATIVE).
The second assertion is the structural guardrail tying the registry-
side PK rule to the adapter-side runtime no-op so they cannot drift.
work_units.summary: Register PK-capability rules for every platform surfaced by the w2 audit as missing coverage

(c) the parallel transaction_primitives rules.
Verify against the w1 migration table before editing each file. Run
